analysis:
This batch contains only test files, so it changes no controls directly.

ServingReadinessTests.swift (head 120-181, 269-305) adds tests for the local diagnostic verdicts (pending, unconfirmed, authorized, blocked):
- A refusal right after connecting is pending.
- A refusal older than refusalMaxAge becomes unconfirmed.
- A coordinator request after the latest status counts as authorized.
- An expired App Attest lease or an explicit untrusted status stays blocked regardless of age.

ProviderAuthorizationConnectionTests.swift (head 46-50, 66-81, 133-248, 313-326) covers:
- A receivedAt parameter on handleTrustStatus.
- A logSinkForTesting hook that captures only public log lines.
- noteCoordinatorRequest.
- Supervision changes: a registration refusal alone never re-registers; refusal staleness stops the unauthorized clock; a routed request resets backoff.

These verdicts are local diagnostics and reconnect heuristics. Per TB-002, local doctor verdicts are not trust evidence. Serving authorization is enforced by the coordinator at routing and final handoff (TB-011, T-053), so these provider-side readiness changes do not grant or extend authorization.

The one availability-relevant behavior is reduced self-recovery. Re-registration now requires a current refusal (within refusalMaxAge) or an expired lease. A stalled coordinator that stops repeating refusals would no longer trigger reconnect. This affects availability only and remains within coordinator-owned policy.

Questions for integration:
- Verify the production implementations in the ServingReadiness source and ProviderLoop. Check that handleTrustStatus's receivedAt defaults to the current time and cannot come from coordinator-supplied data.
- Confirm noteCoordinatorRequest is invoked only on authenticated coordinator inference frames and is ignored while disconnected (head 224-227 tests this).
- Confirm logSinkForTesting cannot be activated in production builds, which could otherwise redirect or expose private-visibility logs.

No regression was identified from the test evidence alone.
